paper.title: Detection of Question-Answer Pairs in Email Conversations
paper.abstract: Studies sentence-level question-answer pairing in asynchronous email conversations. The method uses email-thread structure together with lexical and contextual features to identify which earlier question an answer addresses, providing direct empirical evidence for non-adjacent reply alignment in email.

paper.title: Learning to Align Question and Answer Utterances in Customer Service Conversation with Recurrent Pointer Networks
paper.abstract: Directly models question-answer utterance alignment in multi-round customer-service conversations. A recurrent pointer network exploits conversational context and dependencies among alignments and accommodates empty as well as multiple alignments, providing empirical evidence for responses that do not map one-to-one to prior questions.

paper.title: Forst: A Challenge to the NTCIR-16 QA Lab-PoliInfo-3 Task
paper.abstract: Presents a system for the NTCIR-16 Question Answer Alignment task. It segments questioner and answerer statements and maps individual questions to answers using lexical-overlap and embedding-based information, with alignment directly evaluated against the task gold standard.
paper.venue: Proceedings of the 16th NTCIR Conference on Evaluation of Information Access Technologies

paper.title: Automatic Question-Answer Alignment for Japanese Diverse Local Assembly Minutes
paper.abstract: Targets meeting transcripts in which a participant may ask several questions together and officials subsequently answer the corresponding questions one by one. A two-stage method segments question and answer material and then aligns corresponding units, explicitly addressing multiple competing prior questions rather than assuming adjacency.
paper.venue: 2024 11th International Conference on Advanced Informatics: Concept, Theory and Application (ICAICTA)

paper.title: Using Question-Answer Pairs in Extractive Summarization of Email Conversations
paper.abstract: Integrates automatically detected question-answer pairs into extractive summaries of email conversations and evaluates their contribution to summary quality. It provides indirect empirical validation that identifying cross-message question-answer relations captures salient structure in email threads.

paper.title: Multiple questions in oral proficiency interviews
paper.abstract: Analyzes more than one hundred question/task instances in oral proficiency interviews and documents turns containing multiple questions. It distinguishes different organizations of repeated or multiple questioning and examines how these arise around repair, missing rejoinders, and problematic answers, providing empirical evidence that response scope cannot always be inferred from the immediately preceding question alone.

paper.title: ditlab at the NTCIR-16 QA Lab-PoliInfo-3
paper.abstract: Implements question-answer alignment for governmental assembly minutes by identifying related sentence or paragraph units and comparing questions with candidate answers through several matching features. The output explicitly associates earlier questions with later answers rather than merely labeling dialogue acts.
paper.venue: Proceedings of the 16th NTCIR Conference on Evaluation of Information Access Technologies

paper.title: AKBL at the NTCIR-16 QA Lab-PoliInfo-3 Task
paper.abstract: Addresses Question Answer Alignment in assembly minutes where questions and answers may be presented in batches without explicit correspondence. The system segments question and answer texts into semantically coherent units and uses BM25-based scores with a Hungarian-algorithm assignment to align them.
paper.venue: Proceedings of the 16th NTCIR Conference on Evaluation of Information Access Technologies

paper.title: Overview of the NTCIR-16 QA Lab-PoliInfo-3 Task
paper.abstract: Defines an evaluated Question Answer Alignment task over Japanese assembly minutes. The task extracts topical ranges and correspondences between questions and responses in collective-questioning settings where several questions and answers can occur in batches, supplying independently defined gold and formal system evaluation for alignment.
paper.venue: Proceedings of the 16th NTCIR Conference on Evaluation of Information Access Technologies

paper.title: Hierarchical graph fusion network and a new argumentative dataset for multiparty dialogue discourse parsing
paper.abstract: Studies discourse parsing for multiparty argumentative dialogue, where relationships must be extracted between conversational discourse units. It introduces manually annotated argumentative dialogue datasets and a hierarchical graph-fusion model that combines contextual information to predict discourse structure, providing additional empirical evidence for nonlocal target attachment.

paper.title: Detection of imperative and declarative question–answer pairs in email conversations
paper.abstract: Extends email question-answer detection beyond interrogative sentences to imperative and declarative forms. The sentence-level model uses content, context, and thread-structure features and is evaluated on benchmark email corpora, making it directly relevant to replies that answer requests or propositions not syntactically marked as questions.

paper.title: Annotating Abstract Pronominal Anaphora in the DAD Project
paper.abstract: Presents an annotation scheme for abstract pronominal anaphora in texts and dialogues. Antecedents may be verb phrases, clauses, or larger discourse segments, and the paper reports inter-coder evaluation, providing empirical support for span-based annotation of proposition-like antecedents.

paper.title: A simple but effective model for attachment in discourse parsing with multi-task learning for relation labeling
paper.abstract: Uses a BERT-based pair encoder to predict discourse attachments while jointly learning discourse-relation labels. Importantly for multi-proposition response scope, the representation permits a discourse node to have multiple parents, an empirically relevant property of multiparty conversation that is lost under single-antecedent tree assumptions.

paper.title: Identifying reference to abstract objects in dialogue
paper.abstract: Reports annotation experiments in which annotators identify antecedents for discourse-deictic expressions as unconstrained regions of dialogue text. Annotators show convergence on the identity of abstract antecedent regions, supporting empirical span-based treatment of propositions and discourse segments instead of restricting targets to noun phrases.
paper.venue: 10th Workshop on the Semantics and Pragmatics of Dialogue (BRANDIAL 2006)

paper.title: Degrees of Subjectivity and Their Repercussions in Conversation. The View from Online Interactions
paper.abstract: Studies English Reddit conversations annotated for speech acts and functional-dependence relations connecting discourse segments to preceding material. The analysis relates informational exchanges, answers and clarification requests, and explicit agreement or disagreement to different degrees of subjectivity, providing recent empirical data with explicit response dependencies.
paper.venue: Workshop on Structured Linguistic Data and Evaluation (SLiDE)

paper.title: Resolving Discourse-Deictic Pronouns: A Two-Stage Approach to Do It
paper.abstract: Presents a two-stage system that first detects discourse-deictic pronouns and then resolves them to verbal or clausal antecedents. The empirical evaluation separates detection from antecedent resolution and demonstrates a computational approach to proposition-like target selection beyond entity coreference.
paper.venue: Fourth Joint Conference on Lexical and Computational Semantics (*SEM 2015)

paper.title: Anaphoric Annotation in the ARRAU Corpus
paper.abstract: Describes anaphoric annotation in ARRAU, which includes task-oriented dialogue among its genres. The representation explicitly permits multiple antecedents for ambiguous expressions and discourse antecedents denoting abstract entities such as events, actions, and plans, making it useful for null, ambiguity, and multi-antecedent modeling.

paper.title: Clarifying Intentions in Dialogue: A Corpus Study
paper.abstract: Presents a corpus-based investigation of clarification requests concerning interlocutor intentions. It distinguishes problems of intention recognition from problems of intention adoption and conducts an annotation experiment on naturally occurring candidate clarification sequences, providing empirical evidence about what a clarification targets.

paper.title: Resolving Discourse Deictic Anaphora in Dialogues
paper.abstract: Presents an algorithm for resolving discourse-deictic anaphora in spoken dialogue. It first distinguishes individual, discourse-deictic, and vague uses of pronouns and demonstratives and then resolves discourse-deictic cases against preceding discourse, with empirical evaluation on spoken-dialogue data.

paper.title: Resolving Demonstrative Anaphora in the TRAINS93 Corpus
paper.abstract: Reports empirical annotation and analysis of third-person pronouns and demonstratives in task-oriented TRAINS93 dialogue. The study distinguishes ordinary entity reference from demonstratives whose referents are plans or larger discourse material and motivates a resolver capable of handling both kinds of antecedent.
paper.venue: 2nd Colloquium on Discourse, Anaphora and Reference Resolution

paper.title: Discourse Structure and Dialogue Acts in Multiparty Dialogue: the STAC Corpus
paper.abstract: Introduces the STAC corpus of multi-party strategic chats annotated with full SDRT discourse structures. The data contain interleaved conversational threads and explicit discourse links between elementary discourse units, supplying empirical material for evaluating non-local response attachment rather than only turn-level dialogue acts.

paper.title: Abstract Anaphora Resolution in Danish
paper.abstract: Studies Danish pronouns and deictic expressions that can refer either to individuals or to abstract discourse objects. An adapted resolution algorithm is evaluated on four dialogues drawn from two dialogue collections, providing empirical evidence for dialogue-level abstract antecedent selection.
paper.venue: 1st SIGdial Workshop on Discourse and Dialogue

paper.title: Towards identifying unresolved discussions in student online forums
paper.abstract: Empirically analyzes discussion structures in student online forums to identify unresolved discussions and unanswered questions. The work distinguishes patterns in which questions receive answers from those in which issues remain unresolved, making it relevant to explicit modeling of missing response links.

paper.title: Discourse parsing for multi-party chat dialogues
paper.abstract: Develops a discourse parser for multi-party chat that predicts discourse attachments and relation labels among elementary discourse units. Because the parser must decide which preceding discourse unit a new unit attaches to in threaded and interleaved dialogue, it provides direct computational evidence for response-antecedent selection below the whole-message level.

paper.title: Dialogue Acts, Synchronizing Units, and Anaphora Resolution
paper.abstract: Reports a corpus analysis and a model of anaphora resolution in spontaneous spoken dialogue. The analysis distinguishes nominal antecedents from sentential or discourse-deictic antecedents and from vague cases with no clearly identifiable linguistic antecedent, directly motivating null or unresolved outcomes rather than forced nearest-antecedent attachment.
